title: DSH desktop plugin handoff submission
description: One submission directory per plugin version: handoff.json (this schema) plus the npm-pack tarball it describes. The desktop owner verifies every field against the artifact and the pinned compatibility contract (compat.json) before the version can enter the signed catalog.

packageName.description: Must equal the tarball's package.json name, character for character.

version.description: Stable three-segment version, and it must equal the tarball's package.json version and the submission directory's version segment. The catalog only lists stable releases: prerelease (-rc.1) and build (+meta) segments are refused — publish the stable release instead.

author.description: Who wrote the plugin. The author is not necessarily the submitter — pushing the MR on the author's behalf is fine (submitter.name says who pushed). A plain string with no format enforced: 'sebtang' and 'sebtang@company.example' are both valid.

description.description: One or two sentences, in your own words, saying what the plugin does — this is the text colleagues read when deciding whether to install, and it must agree with the MR description.

type.description: The plugin's category, exactly one of the fixed eleven English slugs above (their Chinese translations live in the MR template and the repo README). Pick the closest fit; 'other' is a last resort.

dshRuntimeVersion.description: SemVer range the plugin was tested against, spelled with the characters the range grammar implements (digits, letters, . - ^ ~ > < = | space, *). Must intersect the version pinned in compat.json at verification time.

dshCommit.description: The deepseek-harness commit you tested against. Must equal compat.json dsh.commit exactly.

desktopVersion.description: The DSH Desktop build you smoke-tested with. Must equal compat.json desktop.version exactly.

file.description: Bare filename of the tarball sitting next to handoff.json (npm pack output). No path separators, no control characters, no backticks.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the tarball bytes. Recomputed by the owner; a mismatch fails the handoff before anything is unpacked.

summary.description: What you actually exercised: the scenarios run and the observed result, in your own words.

changes.description: One-paragraph changelog versus the newest version already listed in the catalog (or 'initial submission').
